subject: DPA: evidence handoff and SCCs mapping for Zephyr Health
messages:
From: Samir Kapoor <samir.kapoor@zephyrhealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redlines + SCCs mapping — initial ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Legal at Zephyr asked me to gather DPA redlines and a short list of evidence we can expect for processor controls (SOC2, data export evidence, subprocessor list).

Attached: Zephyr-DPA-redlines_v1.pdf (our marked-up copy). High level asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood's proposed SCCs mapping and whether you will sign the latest EU Commission SCCs (2021) as controller-to-processor exhibits.
- Provide a draft Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) or commitment date when that will be available.
- Provide a current subprocessor roster + expected lead time for any new subprocessor notices.
- Preferred delivery method for evidence (SharePoint link, secure SFTP, or SOC2 report via portal).

Can Redwood provide a short mutual action plan and an estimated timeline for legal review -> redline counter -> final DPA within 10 business days? We would like to prioritize the contract path as part of the Q4 onboarding plan.

Thanks,
Samir Kapoor
Sr. Procurement Manager
Zephyr Health

Samir / Olga — I reviewed the Zephyr redlines and flagged the following items that will need attention from both sides:

1) Role declaration: we will provide a short clause asserting Redwood acts as processor for the service and will process data only on your documented instructions (we will not flip controller/processor obligations unless contractually agreed).
2) SCCs: Redwood will execute the EU SCCs as an exhibit but requires clarification on which party signs as exporter in multi-tenant scenarios. We propose language to limit scope to customer-controlled data sets.
3) TIA: Attached is a preliminary TIA draft focused on technical and organizational measures and country-specific transfer risk mitigations. We will deliver a more formal TIA within 48 hours for your review.
4) Subprocessors: our standard process is 15 business days notice for new subprocessors; we can provide a CSV export of the current roster and SOC2 reports on request.
5) Data retention / deletion: we propose the deletion window align with the Order Form; typical is 30 days post-contract termination unless otherwise agreed.

Attachments: TIA-draft.docx, SCCs-mapping.xlsx

If Zephyr can confirm the minimal set of redlines they absolutely need to keep, we can triage commercial exceptions and push non-blocking items to an appendix. I am ok with the Thursday sync — Olga, please set time.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
